desc:
A Wix app audit and code review gives you a ranked list of what is wrong, what is risky and what to fix first. Ecom Swift LLC reads your repository, tests your widgets and dashboard, and returns a written report your team can act on straight away.

## What is a Wix app audit?

A Wix app audit is a structured review of an existing app against what Wix expects from apps in the App Market. It covers how the code uses the Wix SDK and APIs, which permissions the app requests, how dashboard pages and site widgets behave, how data is stored and how fast everything loads. The output is a written report where each finding is ranked by the effort to fix it and the impact it has.

## Why a review pays off before you spend more on development

Apps grow in layers. A quick fix here, a copied snippet there, and after a year nobody is sure which parts are safe to touch. Without an outside review, teams tend to build new features on top of weak foundations, then pay for it in bug reports, slow widgets and uninstalls.

An audit turns that uncertainty into a short list. You learn which issues are cosmetic, which put site owner data at risk and which could block an App Market update. That lets you spend development time on the items that matter, instead of guessing.

## How an audit affects your results

An app lives or dies on what happens after install. If the widget makes a storefront feel slow, the site owner removes it. If the dashboard throws an error on first use, they never come back. If permissions look excessive, they hesitate to approve the install at all.

Each of these problems is visible in the code and in a test site long before it shows up in your uninstall numbers. Finding them early protects retention, support time and your standing with Wix reviewers. What the audit cannot do is promise a particular rating or approval outcome, since those depend on many things outside the code.

## What a thorough Wix app review includes

- SDK and API use: current packages, deprecated calls and correct error handling.
- Permissions: whether each requested scope is actually needed.
- Data handling: how collections, backend calls and stored records are structured and protected.
- Dashboard pages: form behavior, empty states, error states and loading.
- Site widgets: load speed, behavior inside the editor and layout on a phone.
- App Market guidelines: listing, pricing and behavior rules your app should follow.
- Wix Design System and accessibility: consistent components, keyboard use and readable contrast.
- Security and privacy: secret storage, input checks and what personal data is kept.
- A fix roadmap: findings grouped into quick wins and larger jobs.

## How we run the review

You send the repository and add Ecom Swift LLC as a collaborator in your Dev Center. We install the app on a development site and use it the way a new site owner would, then read the code with that experience in mind. Your app stays untouched for the whole audit.

The Basic package focuses on SDK use, permissions, data handling and the biggest risks. Standard adds widget speed tests, a phone check, a guideline check and a call to walk through the report. Premium adds design, accessibility, security and privacy review, a fix roadmap with estimates, a few sample fixes and a longer call. Each finding states what we saw, why it matters and what a fix would involve.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Send the real repository, not a trimmed copy, so the review matches production.
- Tell us which problems your users have already reported.
- Share your App Market listing and plan structure, so we can check the app against them.
- Decide in advance who on your team will act on the report.

**Avoid:**
- Fixing things halfway through the review, because the findings will drift from the code.
- Hiding known weak spots, since those are the first places we should look.
- Treating every finding as urgent. The ranking exists so you can begin with the top items.
- Skipping the call if one is included, because the discussion often raises questions the report cannot.

## Who this is for

An app owner who inherited code from a previous developer and needs to know what they actually have. A small team about to add major features that wants the foundation checked first. A founder preparing an App Market update who wants to find problems before a reviewer does.

## What we need from you

Send the repository link, the app name in your Dev Center and a short note on your concerns. Add us as a collaborator, which lets us view the app without sharing any login. We never need your password. If you already have a test site with sample data, tell us, and we will use it.

After the report, you can order help with the top findings, a re-check once your team has made changes, or an extra call for questions.
